Hi Tom — great conversation earlier today. Thanks for walking through the high-level constraints for the air-gapped deployment. Per our call, I wanted to recap the key open items and propose next steps so we can keep momentum on the qualification: 

1) Hardware footprint: you mentioned a preferred HA topology with 2 inference nodes + 1 management node per datacenter, and potential need for GPU headroom for batch jobs. Michael, can you confirm recommended GPU counts for our medium throughput profile?

2) Upgrades & offline ops: LegacyBank prefers a maintenance workflow that supports staggered upgrades with the ability to apply signed artifacts offline. Vivek, I'll need the list of what we require for offline upgrade signing and verification (checksums, signed manifests, tooling).

3) Network & airgap constraints: Tom — can you confirm there is no egress from the secured subnet except via the jump host you described? Also please share the approved jump-host protocol and SFTP/USB transfer process if available.

Attached: redwood_onprem_specs_v2.pdf (hardware and packaging overview). I also dropped a simple topology diagram (hw_topology.png).

Proposed next steps: 
- Michael to reply with GPU recommendations and offline upgrade size estimates (by EOD Mon PT).
- Vivek to share the offline upgrade checklist and required artifacts (by Tue).
- Tom to share the jump-host transfer procedure and any procurement timelines.

If that works, we can schedule a short ops working session this week to walk the offline upgrade flow with your infra team.

Thanks —

Hi Tom / Marissa — following up with the hardware guidance we discussed on the call: 

Summary (Medium throughput / low-latency SLOs):
- Per inference node: 4 x A800-equivalent GPUs (or 8 x SXM with appropriate vRAM if you need larger batch jobs), 768GB host RAM, 2 x 10GbE NICs.
- Management node: 2 vCPUs (or equivalent), 32GB RAM, minimal storage (it hosts the control plane components).
- Disk: NVMe for model cache (1-2 TB per inference node recommended depending on model set).

If you expect peak retraining or large batch reruns on the same cluster, add +1 GPU per node as headroom. In the HA topology Marissa referenced (2 inference + 1 management per DC), that maps to 8 GPUs available for active serving and 4 for redundancy/headroom.

Offline upgrade artifacts: typical signed payload sizes range 50-300 MB depending on model binaries. For model-only updates we often push ~200 MB tarballs. For full runtime+models expect up to 1-2 GB. We support staged upgrades where management node is updated first, then inference nodes in rolling fashion.

I'll attach a one-pager with estimated sizes (included in redwood_onprem_specs_v2.pdf) and can provide a CSV BOM for procurement on request.

Let me know if you want me on the ops session this week — I can walk through the rolling upgrade steps and failure modes.

Thanks,
Michael Grant

Hi Tom — quick security checklist/questions to make sure our on-prem package fits your controls: 

1) Signed artifact verification: we sign release artifacts with an RSA 4096 key and provide SHA-256 checksums. Do you require an HSM-backed key or will a signed manifest plus checksum suffice?

2) Offline bootstrap: we support an offline bootstrap image that your engineers can write to media. Confirm which image delivery mechanism you prefer (SFTP to the jump host, USB in sealed bags, or air-gapped transfer appliance).

3) Key management & secrets: will you provide a KMS/HSM endpoint in the air-gapped environment or do you prefer customer-managed envelope encryption with keys stored offline?

4) Audit/log shipping: for air-gapped ops you mentioned a secure log-bundle export. We'll produce signed log bundles and a verification script — confirm file naming and retention policy (example: logs_YYYYMMDD.tar.gz.sig).

5) Access controls: please confirm the set of service accounts that will have SSH/Jumphost push privileges so we can generate least-privilege runbooks.

If you can share answers inline, we can prepare a formal compliance pack (evidence templates, signed manifests, and an on-site checklist) and aim to deliver that by Wed.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai

Marissa / team — thanks for the clear recap and the spec doc. Quick answers below: 

1) Hardware: procurement prefers quoting for A800-equivalent (4 GPUs per node) with an optional +1 GPU upgrade line item. Please include the CSV BOM as Michael offered.

2) Jump host / transfer: we use an approved jump host that allows SFTP into a staging area; from there the operations team does an integrity check and loads artifacts via USB to the sealed environment. I'll share our transfer SOP PDF with you (procurement redacted certain parts) — attaching the SOP link to our shared Drive.

3) Signing & KMS: the signed manifest + SHA-256 checksums are fine for now. We may require HSM-backed validation later; we'll flag that during the compliance review.

4) Bootstrapping: SFTP -> staging -> USB process is the preferred flow. We will provide the list of service accounts and the persona matrix by Tue EOD.

5) Next steps: please provide the BOM and the formal compliance pack so procurement and InfoSec can review. Can we schedule the ops working session Thu 10:00 AM ET? If that works for you, include Michael and Vivek.
